source.text: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεύς· Εἰ ταῦτα οὕτως ἔχει;

records.literal_gloss: Said then the high priest, If these things so are?

en.L: Then the high priest said, "Are these things so?"
en.B: The high priest asked, "Are these charges true?"
en.R: Then the high priest asked Stephen, "Is this true?"

es.L: Entonces el sumo sacerdote dijo: «¿Son así estas cosas?».
es.B: El sumo sacerdote preguntó: «¿Son ciertas estas acusaciones?».
es.R: Entonces el sumo sacerdote le preguntó a Esteban: «¿Es verdad esto?».

fr.L: Et le grand prêtre dit : « Ces choses sont-elles ainsi ? »
fr.B: Le grand prêtre demanda : « Ces accusations sont-elles fondées ? »
fr.R: Alors le grand prêtre a demandé à Étienne : « Est-ce que c’est vrai ? »

sw.L: Ndipo kuhani mkuu akasema, "Je, mambo haya ndivyo yalivyo?"
sw.B: Kuhani mkuu aliuliza, "Je, mashtaka haya ni ya kweli?"
sw.R: Kisha kuhani mkuu akamwuliza Stefano, "Je, haya ni kweli?"

vi.L: Thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm hỏi: "Những điều này có đúng như vậy không?"
vi.B: Thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm hỏi: "Những lời buộc tội này có đúng không?"
vi.R: Bấy giờ thầy tế lễ thượng phẩm hỏi Ê-tiên: "Có đúng như vậy không?"

ko.L: 그러자 대제사장이 말했다. "이것이 사실이냐?"
ko.B: 대제사장이 물었다. "이 고발이 사실이냐?"
ko.R: 그러자 대제사장이 스데반에게 물었다. "이 말이 사실이냐?"

pt.L: Então o sumo sacerdote disse: "Estas coisas são assim?"
pt.B: O sumo sacerdote perguntou: "Essas acusações são verdadeiras?"
pt.R: Então o sumo sacerdote perguntou a Estêvão: "Isso é verdade?"

am.L: ሊቀ ካህናቱም፦ «ይህ ነገር እንዲህ ነውን?» አለ።
am.B: ሊቀ ካህናቱ፦ «ይህ ክስ እውነት ነውን?» ብሎ ጠየቀ።
am.R: ከዚያም ሊቀ ካህናቱ እስጢፋኖስን፦ «ይህ እውነት ነው?» ብሎ ጠየቀው።

decisions.choice: the high priest: the head of the council before which Stephen stands
decisions.reason: The high priest led the council (5:21, 5:27). Acts does not name him here; Annas and Caiaphas are named among the high priestly family in 4:6.

decisions.choice: are these things so: a direct question whether the charges are true
alternatives: if these things are so (a condition)
decisions.reason: The small word that usually means "if" can introduce a direct question (1:6). "These things" are the charges of 6:13-14, that Stephen spoke against the temple and the law.

decisions.choice: these charges; Stephen
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "these things" are, and Readable names the one asked, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: el sumo sacerdote
decisions.reason: The book-wide term, as in the Gospels: the head of the council before which Stephen stands (m1).

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Gospels: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and as young readers now meet stories. Speech keeps its own tenses. This holds for the whole chapter; for Stephen's speech see 7:2.

decisions.choice: le grand prêtre (no hyphen)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's form for the high priest in every book; "souverain sacrificateur" is the old Protestant term and now obscure.

decisions.choice: the high priest questions Stephen in 해라체; Stephen answers the council in 합쇼체 through his speech (7:2-53), and tells Israel's history in its past tense ("-었습니다")
decisions.reason: As with the apostles before the council (4:7; 5:28): the judge speaks down to the accused, and the accused answers with the courtesy due to the court. Stephen's speech is one long public address, so it keeps the formal polite style even where it turns to rebuke (7:51).

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοὶ καὶ πατέρες, ἀκούσατε· Ὁ θεὸς τῆς δόξης ὤφθη τῷ πατρὶ ἡμῶν Ἀβραὰμ ὄντι ἐν τῇ Μεσοποταμίᾳ πρὶν ἢ κατοικῆσαι αὐτὸν ἐν Χαρράν, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ἔξελθε ἐκ τῆς γῆς σου καὶ ἐκ τῆς συγγενείας σου, καὶ δεῦρο εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἄν σοι δείξω.

records.literal_gloss: He then said, Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of the glory appeared to the father of us Abraham being in the Mesopotamia before rather dwelling him in Haran, \v 3 and said to him, Go out from the land of you and from the kindred of you, and come into the land which ever to you I will show.

en.L: And he said, "Men, brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran, \v 3 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your relatives, and come into the land that I will show you.'
en.B: Stephen replied, "Brothers and fathers, listen. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran. \v 3 God said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your kin, and come to the land that I will show you.'
en.R: Stephen answered, "Brothers and leaders of our people, listen to me. Long ago the God of glory came and showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to Abraham, the father of our nation. At that time Abraham lived in Mesopotamia. He had not yet moved to Haran. \v 3 God said to him, 'Leave your country and your relatives. Go to the land that I will show you.'

es.L: Y él dijo: «Hombres, hermanos y padres, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}}. El Dios de la gloria se apareció a nuestro padre Abraham cuando estaba en Mesopotamia, antes de que habitara en Harán, \v 3 y le dijo: “Sal de tu tierra y de tus parientes, y ven a la tierra que yo te muestre”.
es.B: Esteban respondió: «Hermanos y padres, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}}. El Dios de la gloria se apareció a nuestro padre Abraham cuando aún estaba en Mesopotamia, antes de que se estableciera en Harán. \v 3 Dios le dijo: “Deja tu tierra y a tu familia, y ven a la tierra que yo te indicaré”.
es.R: Esteban contestó: «Hermanos y líderes de nuestro pueblo, {{plural_you:escúchenme|escuchadme}}. Hace mucho tiempo, el Dios de la gloria vino y se mostró a Abraham, el padre de nuestra nación. En ese tiempo Abraham vivía en Mesopotamia. Todavía no se había ido a vivir a Harán. \v 3 Dios le dijo: “Deja tu país y a tus parientes. Ve a la tierra que yo te mostraré”.

fr.L: Et il déclara : « Hommes, frères et pères, écoutez. Le Dieu de gloire est apparu à notre père Abraham quand il était en Mésopotamie, avant qu’il habite à Harân, \v 3 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui a dit : “Sors de ton pays et de ta parenté, et viens dans le pays que je te montrerai.”
fr.B: Étienne répondit : « Frères et pères, écoutez. Le Dieu de gloire est apparu à notre père Abraham alors qu’il était encore en Mésopotamie, avant qu’il s’installe à Harân. \v 3 Dieu lui a dit : “Quitte ton pays et ta famille, et va dans le pays que je te montrerai.”
fr.R: Étienne a répondu : « Frères, et vous, les responsables de notre peuple, écoutez-moi. Il y a très longtemps, le Dieu de gloire est venu {{deity_pronoun:se|Se}} montrer à Abraham, le père de notre nation. À ce moment-là, Abraham vivait en Mésopotamie. Il n’était pas encore parti s’installer à Harân. \v 3 Dieu lui a dit : “Quitte ton pays et ta famille. Va dans le pays que je vais te montrer.”

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Wanaume, ndugu na akina baba, sikilizeni. Mungu wa utukufu alimtokea baba yetu Ibrahimu alipokuwa katika Mesopotamia, kabla hajakaa Harani, \v 3 akamwambia, 'Toka katika nchi yako na kutoka kwa jamaa zako, uje katika nchi nitakayokuonyesha.'
sw.B: Stefano alijibu, "Ndugu zangu na akina baba, sikilizeni. Mungu wa utukufu alimtokea baba yetu Ibrahimu alipokuwa bado Mesopotamia, kabla hajaenda kukaa Harani. \v 3 Mungu alimwambia, 'Toka katika nchi yako na kwa jamaa zako, uende katika nchi nitakayokuonyesha.'
sw.R: Stefano akajibu, "Ndugu zangu na viongozi wa watu wetu, nisikilizeni. Zamani sana Mungu wa utukufu alikuja akajionyesha kwa Ibrahimu, baba wa taifa letu. Wakati huo Ibrahimu aliishi Mesopotamia. Alikuwa bado hajahamia Harani. \v 3 Mungu alimwambia, 'Iache nchi yako na jamaa zako. Nenda katika nchi nitakayokuonyesha.'

vi.L: Ê-tiên nói: "Thưa các anh em và các bậc cha ông, xin hãy nghe. Đức Chúa Trời vinh quang đã hiện ra với tổ phụ chúng ta là Áp-ra-ham khi ông còn ở Mê-sô-pô-ta-mi, trước khi ông đến cư ngụ tại Cha-ran, \v 3 và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với ông: 'Hãy ra khỏi xứ sở con và khỏi bà con con, mà đi đến xứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ chỉ cho con.'
vi.B: Ê-tiên đáp: "Thưa anh em và các bậc cha chú, xin hãy nghe tôi. Đức Chúa Trời vinh quang đã hiện ra với tổ phụ chúng ta là Áp-ra-ham khi ông còn ở Mê-sô-pô-ta-mi, trước khi ông đến sống tại Cha-ran. \v 3 Đức Chúa Trời phán với ông: 'Hãy rời bỏ quê hương và họ hàng của con, mà đi đến xứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ chỉ cho con.'
vi.R: Ê-tiên trả lời: "Thưa anh em và các vị lãnh đạo của dân tộc chúng ta, xin hãy nghe tôi. Từ rất lâu, Đức Chúa Trời vinh quang đã đến và tỏ mình ra cho Áp-ra-ham, là tổ phụ của dân tộc chúng ta. Lúc ấy Áp-ra-ham đang sống ở Mê-sô-pô-ta-mi. Ông chưa dời đến Cha-ran. \v 3 Đức Chúa Trời phán với ông: 'Hãy rời bỏ quê hương và họ hàng của con. Hãy đi đến xứ mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ chỉ cho con.'

ko.L: 그가 말했다. "형제 여러분, 그리고 아버지 여러분, 들으십시오. 영광의 하나님께서 우리 조상 아브라함이 하란에 살기 전, 메소포타미아에 있을 때에 그에게 나타나셔서 \v 3 그에게 말씀하셨습니다. '너는 네 땅과 네 친척을 떠나, 내가 너에게 보여 줄 땅으로 가거라.'
ko.B: 스데반이 대답했다. "형제 여러분, 그리고 아버지 여러분, 들어 주십시오. 우리 조상 아브라함이 하란에 자리 잡기 전, 아직 메소포타미아에 있을 때에 영광의 하나님께서 그에게 나타나셨습니다. \v 3 하나님께서 그에게 말씀하셨습니다. '네 땅과 네 친척을 떠나, 내가 너에게 보여 줄 땅으로 가거라.'
ko.R: 스데반이 대답했다. "형제 여러분, 그리고 우리 백성의 어른 여러분, 내 말을 들어 주십시오. 오래전에 영광의 하나님께서 우리 민족의 조상 아브라함에게 나타나셨습니다. 그때 아브라함은 메소포타미아에 살고 있었습니다. 아직 하란으로 옮겨 가기 전이었습니다. \v 3 하나님께서 아브라함에게 말씀하셨습니다. '네 나라와 네 친척을 떠나라. 내가 너에게 보여 줄 땅으로 가거라.'

pt.L: E ele disse: "Homens, irmãos e pais, ouçam. O Deus da glória apareceu ao nosso pai Abraão quando ele estava na Mesopotâmia, antes de morar em Harã, \v 3 e lhe disse: 'Sai da tua terra e da tua parentela e vem para a terra que eu te mostrar.'
pt.B: Estêvão respondeu: "Irmãos e pais, ouçam. O Deus da glória apareceu ao nosso pai Abraão quando ele ainda estava na Mesopotâmia, antes de se estabelecer em Harã. \v 3 Deus lhe disse: 'Deixa a tua terra e os teus parentes e vai para a terra que eu te mostrarei.'
pt.R: Estêvão respondeu: "Irmãos e líderes do nosso povo, escutem o que eu digo. Há muito tempo, o Deus da glória veio e se mostrou a Abraão, o pai da nossa nação. Naquele tempo Abraão morava na Mesopotâmia. Ele ainda não tinha se mudado para Harã. \v 3 Deus lhe disse: 'Deixa o teu país e os teus parentes. Vai para a terra que eu vou te mostrar.'

am.L: እርሱም እንዲህ አለ፦ «ወንድሞችና አባቶች ሆይ፣ ስሙ። የክብር አምላክ ለአባታችን ለአብርሃም በካራን ከመኖሩ በፊት በመስጴጦምያ ሳለ ተገለጠለት፤ \v 3 እንዲህም አለው፦ “ከአገርህና ከዘመዶችህ ውጣ፤ እኔም ወደማሳይህ አገር ና።”
am.B: እስጢፋኖስም እንዲህ ሲል መለሰ፦ «ወንድሞችና አባቶች ሆይ፣ ስሙ። የክብር አምላክ ለአባታችን ለአብርሃም በካራን ከመቀመጡ በፊት ገና በመስጴጦምያ ሳለ ተገለጠለት። \v 3 እግዚአብሔርም፦ “ከአገርህና ከዘመዶችህ ተለይተህ ውጣ፤ እኔ ወደማሳይህም አገር ሂድ” አለው።
am.R: እስጢፋኖስም እንዲህ ብሎ መለሰ፦ «ወንድሞቼና የሕዝባችን መሪዎች ሆይ፣ ስሙኝ። ከብዙ ዘመን በፊት የክብር አምላክ ለሕዝባችን አባት ለአብርሃም ተገለጠለት። በዚያን ጊዜ አብርሃም የሚኖረው በመስጴጦምያ ነበር፤ ገና ወደ ካራን አልሄደም ነበር። \v 3 እግዚአብሔርም፦ “አገርህንና ዘመዶችህን ትተህ ውጣ። እኔ ወደማሳይህ አገር ሂድ” አለው።

decisions.choice: men, brothers and fathers: a formal address to the council, honoring its older members as fathers
alternatives: an address to men and women
decisions.reason: Stephen speaks to the council (6:12, 6:15), whose members were all men, so the address is not widened to men and women, as with Gamaliel's address to the council (5:35). "Fathers" honors the elders and leaders among them; Paul opens his speech to a Jerusalem crowd with "brothers and fathers" (22:1).

decisions.choice: the God of glory: God who shows himself in his glory
alternatives: the glorious God, without the sense of appearing
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Psalm 29:3. The God who "appeared" is the God whose glory is seen, and the speech ends with Stephen seeing the glory of God (7:55).

decisions.choice: Abraham was called while in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran
alternatives: the call came in Haran, as the order of Genesis 11:31-12:4 might suggest
decisions.reason: Genesis 11:31 tells how Terah took Abram from Ur of the Chaldeans to Haran, and the call of Genesis 12:1 is told after that, with Abram leaving Haran (12:4). Stephen places God's appearing before Haran, in Mesopotamia, which 7:4 calls the land of the Chaldeans. Genesis 15:7 and Nehemiah 9:7 say that God brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and Joshua 24:2-3 that God took him from beyond the river. Genesis does not report a call in Ur in so many words. The text is translated as it stands, without settling how the two accounts fit together.

decisions.choice: God's words are Genesis 12:1
alternatives: a summary in Stephen's own words
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 12:1 closely, but leave out "and from your father's house".

decisions.choice: Brothers and fathers
decisions.reason: Balanced drops the formal opening word "men", which English does not use in this kind of address; Literal keeps it. No gender setting applies, since the hearers were all men.

decisions.choice: leaders of our people
decisions.reason: Readable says whom "fathers" honors here, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: came and showed himself; the father of our nation
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "appeared" means and in what sense Abraham is "our father".

decisions.choice: Hombres, hermanos y padres (L); Hermanos y padres (B); Hermanos y líderes de nuestro pueblo (R)
decisions.reason: A formal address to the council that honours its older members as fathers (m1). Literal keeps all three words, with the everyday "hombres" rather than the older "varones"; Balanced leaves out "Hombres", as the English does, and Readable says who the "fathers" are.

decisions.choice: le dijo, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves out a subject pronoun the verb already shows, so where the English has a span on "he" for God there is nothing to capitalise (here and through the chapter). Object and possessive pronouns for God keep the span ("me", "mi", "le").

decisions.choice: Stephen's speech, including his account of Israel's history (7:2-50), in the passé composé at every level, as speech
alternatives: the history (7:2-50) in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps the tenses of speech at every level, including a story told inside a speech, and Stephen is speaking to the council. So his retelling of Israel's history is in the passé composé (with the imparfait and plus-que-parfait where French needs them), as are the retellings in the speeches of Acts 13, 22 and 26. The narrative frame around the speech (7:1-2a, 7:54-60) follows the chapter's narrative rule.

decisions.choice: Harân
decisions.reason: The usual modern French spelling of the town; "Charan" is the older form of Louis Segond.

decisions.choice: Wanaume, ndugu na akina baba (L); Ndugu zangu na akina baba (B); Ndugu zangu na viongozi wa watu wetu (R)
decisions.reason: A formal address to the council that honors its older members as fathers (meaning decision on the address). "Akina baba" is the respectful way to address a group of fathers or older men; "wazee" would sound like the elders as an office. As in Acts 13:15, Balanced drops "wanaume", which Swahili does not need beside "ndugu"; Readable says who the fathers are, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives in this chapter
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("akamwambia", "alimhamisha", "wataniabudu"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the deity_pronoun setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives ("watu wangu", "nami", "kiti changu cha enzi"); Swahili has fewer spans than English here.

decisions.choice: "Thưa anh em và các bậc cha ông" (L), "các bậc cha chú" (B), "các vị lãnh đạo của dân tộc chúng ta" (R); Stephen says "tôi", "chúng ta" for Israel and "các ông" to the council (7:2-53)
decisions.reason: A formal address to the council that honours its older members as fathers (meaning decision). "các bậc cha chú" is the respectful Vietnamese way to address the elders of one's own people. "các ông" is the "you" the apostles use before the council (4:8).

decisions.choice: God speaks to Abraham as "con" and says "Ta"
decisions.reason: The form of the Vietnamese Galatians 3:8 for God's words to Abraham.

decisions.choice: "Cha-ran", "Mê-sô-pô-ta-mi"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms of the place names.

decisions.choice: "형제 여러분, 그리고 아버지 여러분" (L, B); "형제 여러분, 그리고 우리 백성의 어른 여러분" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: A formal address to the council, honoring its older members as fathers (meaning decision); the English has no setting here. Readable says what "fathers" means, as the English Readable says "leaders of our people".

decisions.choice: God speaks in 해라체 with "나" and "너" in the quotations of Stephen's speech ("가거라")
decisions.reason: As the style guide gives for God speaking (section 7a), and as in 2:17.

decisions.choice: tu for God's words to Abraham
decisions.reason: God speaking to a person uses "tu" (style guide, section 4), as in all the Old Testament words Stephen quotes in this speech (7:3, 7:7, 7:33-34). The people in the story speak to one another with "você" (7:26-28, 7:35).

decisions.choice: Homens, irmãos e pais (L); Irmãos e pais (B); Irmãos e líderes do nosso povo (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the council were all men (m1), so no gender setting; Readable says whom "pais" honours. Stephen then speaks to the council as "os senhores" (see 7:4).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns and verb endings for God in Stephen's speech are written once, with no span.

decisions.choice: ወንድሞችና አባቶች ሆይ (Men, brothers and fathers)
decisions.reason: 'Men, brothers' is a formal Greek opening; Amharic addresses a gathering with the nouns and ሆይ, and a separate 'men' would sound odd, so it is left out, as elsewhere in Acts. The address is to the council, so it has no gender setting, as in the English. Readable says 'leaders of our people' for 'fathers', as the English does.

source.text: τότε ἐξελθὼν ἐκ γῆς Χαλδαίων κατῴκησεν ἐν Χαρράν.

records.literal_gloss: Then having gone out from [the] land of Chaldeans he dwelt in Haran.

en.L: Then, going out from [the] land of [the] Chaldeans, he lived in Haran.
en.B: So he left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran.
en.R: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and went to live in Haran.

es.L: Entonces, saliendo de [la] tierra de [los] caldeos, habitó en Harán.
es.B: Así que salió de la tierra de los caldeos y se estableció en Harán.
es.R: Entonces Abraham dejó la tierra de los caldeos y se fue a vivir a Harán.

fr.L: Alors, sortant du pays des Chaldéens, il a habité à Harân.
fr.B: Il a donc quitté le pays des Chaldéens et s’est établi à Harân.
fr.R: Alors Abraham a quitté le pays des Chaldéens et il est allé vivre à Harân.

sw.L: Kisha, akiisha kutoka katika nchi ya Wakaldayo, alikaa Harani.
sw.B: Basi aliondoka katika nchi ya Wakaldayo, akaenda kukaa Harani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Ibrahimu aliondoka katika nchi ya Wakaldayo, akaenda kuishi Harani.

vi.L: Bấy giờ ông ra khỏi xứ của người Canh-đê và đến cư ngụ tại Cha-ran.
vi.B: Vậy ông rời xứ của người Canh-đê và đến sống tại Cha-ran.
vi.R: Vì vậy Áp-ra-ham rời bỏ xứ của người Canh-đê và đến sống tại Cha-ran.

ko.L: 그때 그는 갈대아 사람들의 땅을 떠나 하란에 살았습니다.
ko.B: 그래서 아브라함은 갈대아 사람들의 땅을 떠나 하란에 자리 잡았습니다.
ko.R: 그래서 아브라함은 갈대아 사람들의 땅을 떠나 하란으로 가서 살았습니다.

pt.L: Então, saindo da terra dos caldeus, morou em Harã.
pt.B: Assim ele deixou a terra dos caldeus e se estabeleceu em Harã.
pt.R: Então Abraão saiu da terra dos caldeus e foi morar em Harã.

am.L: ከዚያም ከከለዳውያን አገር ወጥቶ በካራን ተቀመጠ።
am.B: ስለዚህ ከከለዳውያን ምድር ወጥቶ በካራን መኖር ጀመረ።
am.R: ስለዚህ አብርሃም የከለዳውያንን ምድር ትቶ በካራን ለመኖር ሄደ።

decisions.choice: the land of the Chaldeans: southern Mesopotamia, the region of Ur
decisions.reason: Genesis calls Abram's first home "Ur of the Chaldeans" (Genesis 11:28, 11:31). Haran lay far to the northwest, on the way to Canaan.

decisions.choice: Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject.

decisions.choice: "갈대아", "하란"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms of the names (style guide, Settled).

source.text: κἀκεῖθεν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ μετῴκισεν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν γῆν ταύτην εἰς ἣν ὑμεῖς νῦν κατοικεῖτε, καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κληρονομίαν ἐν αὐτῇ οὐδὲ βῆμα ποδός, καὶ ἐπηγγείλατο δοῦναι αὐτῷ εἰς κατάσχεσιν αὐτὴν καὶ τῷ σπέρματι αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτόν, οὐκ ὄντος αὐτῷ τέκνου.

records.literal_gloss: And from there after the to die the father of him He removed him into the land this in which you now dwell, \v 5 and not He gave to him an inheritance in it, not even [the] step of a foot, and He promised to give to him for a possession it and to the seed of him after him, not being to him a child.

en.L: And from there, after his father died, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved him into this land in which you now live. \v 5 And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him no inheritance in it, not even [the] step of a foot, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his seed after him, while he had no child.
en.B: After his father's death, God moved him from there into this land where you now live. \v 5 He gave him no share of it to inherit, not even ground enough for one step. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised to give it to him and to his descendants after him to hold as their own, while Abraham was still childless.
en.R: After Abraham's father died, God brought Abraham to this land where you live now. \v 5 God did not give him any of the land to own, not even a small piece. But God promised that one day the land would belong to Abraham and to his family after him. God promised this even though Abraham did not have any children yet.

es.L: Y de allí, después de morir su padre, lo trasladó a esta tierra en la que {{plural_you:ustedes habitan|vosotros habitáis}} ahora. \v 5 Y no le dio herencia en ella, ni siquiera [el] paso de un pie, y prometió dársela en posesión a él y a su simiente después de él, cuando él no tenía hijo.
es.B: Después de la muerte de su padre, Dios lo trasladó de allí a esta tierra donde {{plural_you:ustedes viven|vosotros vivís}} ahora. \v 5 No le dio en ella ninguna parte como herencia, ni siquiera el terreno que ocupa un pie. Pero le prometió que se la daría en posesión a él y a sus descendientes después de él, cuando Abraham aún no tenía hijos.
es.R: Después de que murió el padre de Abraham, Dios trajo a Abraham a esta tierra donde {{plural_you:ustedes viven|vosotros vivís}} ahora. \v 5 Dios no le dio nada de esta tierra como propiedad, ni siquiera un pedacito. Pero Dios prometió que un día la tierra sería de Abraham y de su familia después de él. Dios le prometió esto aunque Abraham todavía no tenía hijos.

fr.L: Et de là, après que son père est mort, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a fait passer dans ce pays où vous habitez maintenant. \v 5 Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne lui y a donné aucun héritage, pas même [la longueur d’]un pas, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis de le lui donner en possession, ainsi qu’à sa descendance après lui, alors qu’il n’avait pas d’enfant.
fr.B: Après la mort de son père, Dieu l’a fait passer de là dans ce pays où vous habitez aujourd’hui. \v 5 Il ne lui en a donné aucune part en héritage, pas même la place d’un seul pas. Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a promis de le lui donner en propriété, à lui et à sa descendance après lui, alors qu’Abraham n’avait pas encore d’enfant.
fr.R: Après la mort du père d’Abraham, Dieu a conduit Abraham dans ce pays où vous habitez maintenant. \v 5 Dieu ne lui a donné aucune partie de ce pays, pas même un petit morceau de terrain. Mais Dieu a promis qu’un jour le pays appartiendrait à Abraham et à sa famille après lui. Dieu a promis cela alors qu’Abraham n’avait encore aucun enfant.

sw.L: Na kutoka huko, baada ya kufa kwa baba yake, alimhamisha mpaka nchi hii mnayoikaa ninyi sasa. \v 5 Wala hakumpa urithi ndani yake, hata hatua ya mguu, lakini aliahidi kumpa iwe milki yake, na ya uzao wake baada yake, ingawa hakuwa na mtoto.
sw.B: Baada ya kifo cha baba yake, Mungu alimhamisha kutoka huko akamleta katika nchi hii mnayoishi sasa. \v 5 Hakumpa sehemu yoyote ya nchi hii iwe urithi wake, hata mahali pa kuweka mguu mmoja. Lakini aliahidi kumpa nchi hiyo iwe milki yake na ya wazao wake baada yake, ingawa wakati huo Ibrahimu hakuwa na mtoto.
sw.R: Baba yake Ibrahimu alipokufa, Mungu alimleta Ibrahimu katika nchi hii mnayoishi sasa. \v 5 Mungu hakumpa sehemu yoyote ya nchi hii iwe mali yake, hata kipande kidogo. Lakini Mungu aliahidi kwamba siku moja nchi hii ingekuwa mali ya Ibrahimu na ya wazao wake baada yake. Mungu aliahidi hivyo ingawa Ibrahimu alikuwa bado hana mtoto yeyote.

vi.L: Từ đó, sau khi cha ông qua đời, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dời ông đến xứ này là nơi các ông hiện đang ở. \v 5 Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không cho ông một phần sản nghiệp nào trong xứ này, dù chỉ một chỗ đặt chân; nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hứa ban xứ ấy làm sở hữu cho ông và cho dòng dõi ông sau này, dù lúc ấy ông chưa có con.
vi.B: Sau khi cha ông qua đời, Đức Chúa Trời đã đưa ông từ đó đến xứ này, là nơi các ông đang sống bây giờ. \v 5 Ngài không cho ông một phần đất nào để làm sản nghiệp, dù chỉ một chỗ đặt chân. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hứa sẽ ban xứ này cho ông và cho dòng dõi ông sau này làm sở hữu, trong khi Áp-ra-ham vẫn chưa có con.
vi.R: Sau khi cha của Áp-ra-ham qua đời, Đức Chúa Trời đưa Áp-ra-ham đến xứ này, là nơi các ông đang sống bây giờ. \v 5 Đức Chúa Trời không cho ông một phần đất nào để làm của riêng, dù chỉ một mảnh nhỏ. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời hứa rằng một ngày kia xứ này sẽ thuộc về Áp-ra-ham và gia đình ông sau này. Đức Chúa Trời hứa như vậy dù lúc ấy Áp-ra-ham chưa có con.

ko.L: 그리고 그의 아버지가 죽은 뒤에, 하나님께서 그를 거기서 여러분이 지금 살고 있는 이 땅으로 옮기셨습니다. \v 5 그러나 하나님께서는 이 땅에서 그에게 유산을 주지 않으셨습니다. 발 디딜 만한 땅도 주지 않으셨습니다. 그러나 그에게 아직 자식이 없었는데도, 이 땅을 그와 그 뒤의 씨에게 소유로 주시겠다고 약속하셨습니다.
ko.B: 아브라함의 아버지가 죽은 뒤에, 하나님께서는 그를 거기서 여러분이 지금 살고 있는 이 땅으로 옮기셨습니다. \v 5 그러나 하나님께서는 이 땅에서 그에게 유산을 조금도 주지 않으셨습니다. 발 디딜 만한 땅조차 주지 않으셨습니다. 그 대신에, 아직 아브라함에게 자식이 없었는데도, 이 땅을 그와 그의 자손에게 소유로 주시겠다고 약속하셨습니다.
ko.R: 아브라함의 아버지가 죽은 뒤에, 하나님께서는 아브라함을 여러분이 지금 사는 이 땅으로 데려오셨습니다. \v 5 하나님께서는 이 땅에서 아브라함에게 아주 작은 땅도 주지 않으셨습니다. 그러나 언젠가 이 땅이 아브라함과 그의 자손의 것이 될 것이라고 약속하셨습니다. 그때 아브라함에게는 아직 자식이 하나도 없었는데도 하나님께서 그렇게 약속하셨습니다.

pt.L: E dali, depois que o pai dele morreu, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} o mudou para esta terra em que os senhores agora habitam. \v 5 E não lhe deu herança nela, nem sequer [o] espaço de um pé, e prometeu dá-la como propriedade a ele e à sua descendência depois dele, quando ele não tinha filho.
pt.B: Depois da morte do pai dele, Deus o trouxe dali para esta terra onde os senhores agora vivem. \v 5 Não lhe deu nela nenhuma herança, nem mesmo o chão para pôr um pé. Mas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} prometeu dar a terra a ele e aos seus descendentes depois dele, como propriedade, quando Abraão ainda não tinha filhos.
pt.R: Depois que o pai de Abraão morreu, Deus trouxe Abraão para esta terra onde os senhores vivem agora. \v 5 Deus não deu a ele nenhum pedaço da terra, nem mesmo um pedacinho. Mas Deus prometeu que um dia a terra ia pertencer a Abraão e à família dele depois dele. Deus prometeu isso quando Abraão ainda não tinha nenhum filho.

am.L: ከዚያም አባቱ ከሞተ በኋላ እናንተ አሁን ወደምትኖሩባት ወደዚህች ምድር አፈለሰው፤ \v 5 በእርሷም የእግር መርገጫ ያህል እንኳ ርስት አልሰጠውም፤ ልጅም ሳይኖረው ለእርሱና ከእርሱ በኋላ ለዘሩ ይዞታ አድርጎ ሊሰጣት ተስፋ ሰጠው።
am.B: አባቱ ከሞተ በኋላ እግዚአብሔር ከዚያ አሁን እናንተ ወደምትኖሩባት ወደዚህች ምድር አመጣው። \v 5 በእርሷም አንድ እርምጃ የሚያህል መሬት እንኳ ርስት አድርጎ አልሰጠውም። ነገር ግን አብርሃም ገና ልጅ ሳይኖረው ምድሪቱን ለእርሱና ከእርሱ በኋላ ለሚመጡት ዘሮቹ ይዞታ አድርጎ እንደሚሰጥ ተስፋ ሰጠው።
am.R: የአብርሃም አባት ከሞተ በኋላ እግዚአብሔር አብርሃምን አሁን እናንተ ወደምትኖሩባት ወደዚህች ምድር አመጣው። \v 5 እግዚአብሔር ከዚህች ምድር ትንሽ ቁራጭ እንኳ የራሱ እንድትሆን አልሰጠውም። ነገር ግን አንድ ቀን ምድሪቱ የአብርሃምና ከእርሱ በኋላ የሚመጣው ቤተሰቡ እንደምትሆን እግዚአብሔር ተስፋ ሰጠ። አብርሃም ገና ልጆች ባይኖሩትም እግዚአብሔር ይህን ተስፋ ሰጠው።

decisions.choice: Abraham left Haran after his father died
alternatives: Abraham left while his father was still alive
decisions.reason: Genesis 11:26 says Terah was seventy when he fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran; 11:32 says he died in Haran at 205; 12:4 says Abram was seventy-five when he left Haran. Taken together, and if Abram was the firstborn, these would have Terah still alive when Abram left. Genesis tells of Terah's death (11:32) before Abram's leaving (12:4), and Stephen follows that order. The Samaritan Pentateuch gives Terah's age at death in 11:32 as 145, which agrees with Stephen's order. Reviewers should check the Samaritan figure. The text does not explain more, and nothing is added to harmonize it.

decisions.choice: not even the step of a foot: not the smallest piece of ground
decisions.reason: The phrase comes from Deuteronomy 2:5 in the Greek Old Testament. Abraham later bought a field with a cave to bury Sarah (Genesis 23), but that was a purchase, not land given him to inherit.

decisions.choice: God's promise of the land to Abraham and his descendants
decisions.reason: Genesis 12:7, 13:15 and 17:8 promise the land to Abraham and his offspring; Genesis 17:8 and 48:4 call it a possession. The promise was made while Abraham had no son (Genesis 15:2-3).

decisions.choice: seed: descendants
decisions.reason: The singular word here means Abraham's offspring as a whole, as the next verse shows (7:6).

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the one who moved Abraham; the Greek verb has no stated subject.

decisions.choice: God promised this even though
decisions.reason: Readable makes the closing phrase its own sentence.

decisions.choice: simiente (L); descendientes (B); su familia (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of seed, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable say plainly that descendants are meant (m4). "Simiente" returns in 7:6 at Literal.

decisions.choice: sa descendance (L)
decisions.reason: English Literal keeps "seed", but French "semence" is not used for a person's offspring and would read as agricultural; "descendance" is the plain French word for it (m4), and "postérité" is old-fashioned.

decisions.choice: "발 디딜 만한 땅" for "the step of a foot"; "씨" (L), "자손" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Not the smallest piece of ground (meaning decision); "발 디딜 만한" keeps the foot in a natural Korean phrase. Seed means descendants (meaning decision), as in 3:25.

decisions.choice: os senhores
decisions.reason: Stephen speaks to the council, the highest Jewish court, so he addresses its members as "os senhores" throughout the speech, as Peter does in 5:30; it is how Brazilians address a court, and it stays even where he accuses them (7:51-53).

decisions.choice: descendência
decisions.reason: "Semente" for offspring is not natural Portuguese; "descendência" keeps the singular collective of the Greek.

decisions.choice: ዘር (L); ዘሮች (B)
decisions.reason: ዘር, 'seed', is used in Amharic for a man's descendants as in the Greek, so Literal keeps it and Balanced uses its plural, 'descendants'; Readable says 'his family after him', as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἐλάλησεν δὲ οὕτως ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα αὐτοῦ πάροικον ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, καὶ δουλώσουσιν αὐτὸ καὶ κακώσουσιν ἔτη τετρακόσια·

records.literal_gloss: Spoke however thus the God, that will be the seed of him a sojourner in a land foreign, and they will enslave it and will mistreat years four hundred;

en.L: But God spoke in this way, that his seed would be a sojourner in a foreign land, and they would enslave it and mistreat [it] 400 years.
en.B: This is what God said: his descendants would live as outsiders in a land that belonged to others, and its people would make them slaves and treat them harshly for 400 years.
en.R: God also told Abraham that his family after him would live in a country that was not theirs. The people there would make them slaves and treat them badly for 400 years.

es.L: Pero Dios habló de esta manera: que su simiente sería forastera en una tierra extraña, y que la harían esclava y la maltratarían cuatrocientos años.
es.B: Esto es lo que dijo Dios: sus descendientes vivirían como extranjeros en un país que pertenecía a otros, y la gente de allí los haría esclavos y los trataría con dureza durante cuatrocientos años.
es.R: Dios también le dijo a Abraham que su familia después de él viviría en un país que no era suyo. La gente de allí los haría esclavos y los trataría mal durante cuatrocientos años.

fr.L: Or Dieu a parlé ainsi : sa descendance séjournerait en étrangère dans une terre étrangère, et ils la réduiraient en esclavage et la maltraiteraient quatre cents ans.
fr.B: Voici ce que Dieu a déclaré : sa descendance vivrait en étrangère dans un pays qui appartenait à d’autres, et les gens de ce pays en feraient des esclaves et la maltraiteraient pendant quatre cents ans.
fr.R: Dieu a aussi dit à Abraham que sa famille, après lui, vivrait dans un pays qui n’était pas le sien. Les gens de ce pays feraient d’eux des esclaves et les traiteraient mal pendant quatre cents ans.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu alisema hivi, kwamba uzao wake ungekuwa mgeni katika nchi ya kigeni, nao wangeufanya kuwa mtumwa na kuutesa miaka mia nne.
sw.B: Mungu alisema hivi: wazao wake wangeishi kama wageni katika nchi ya watu wengine, na wenyeji wa nchi hiyo wangewafanya watumwa na kuwatendea ukatili kwa miaka mia nne.
sw.R: Mungu alimwambia Ibrahimu pia kwamba wazao wake wangeishi katika nchi isiyo yao. Watu wa nchi hiyo wangewafanya watumwa na kuwatesa kwa miaka mia nne.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời đã phán như vầy: dòng dõi ông sẽ làm kiều dân trên đất khách, và người ta sẽ bắt họ làm nô lệ và hành hạ họ trong bốn trăm năm.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời phán thế này: dòng dõi ông sẽ sống như những người ngoại kiều tại một xứ không phải của mình, và dân xứ ấy sẽ bắt họ làm nô lệ và đối xử tàn tệ với họ trong bốn trăm năm.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời cũng nói với Áp-ra-ham rằng con cháu ông sẽ sống trong một nước không phải của họ. Dân nước ấy sẽ bắt họ làm nô lệ và đối xử tệ với họ trong bốn trăm năm.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다. 그의 씨가 남의 땅에서 나그네가 될 것이고, 그들이 그 씨를 종으로 삼아 사백 년 동안 학대할 것이라고 하셨습니다.
ko.B: 하나님께서는 또 이렇게 말씀하셨습니다. 아브라함의 자손이 남의 나라에서 나그네로 살 것이고, 그 나라 사람들이 그들을 종으로 삼아 사백 년 동안 괴롭힐 것이라는 말씀이었습니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 또 아브라함에게, 그의 자손이 자기들의 나라가 아닌 곳에서 살게 될 것이라고 말씀하셨습니다. 그곳 사람들은 그들을 종으로 부리고 사백 년 동안 못살게 굴 것이었습니다.

pt.L: Mas Deus falou assim: que a descendência dele seria estrangeira em terra alheia, e que a escravizariam e maltratariam por quatrocentos anos.
pt.B: Deus disse assim: os descendentes dele viveriam como estrangeiros numa terra que pertencia a outros, e o povo dessa terra os escravizaria e os trataria com crueldade por quatrocentos anos.
pt.R: Deus também disse a Abraão que a família dele, depois dele, ia morar num país que não era seu. As pessoas de lá iam fazer deles escravos e iam tratá-los mal durante quatrocentos anos.

am.L: እግዚአብሔርም ዘሩ በባዕድ ምድር መጻተኛ እንደሚሆን፣ ባሪያ እንደሚያደርጉትና 400 ዓመት እንደሚያንገላቱት በዚህ መንገድ ተናገረ።
am.B: እግዚአብሔር የተናገረውም ይህ ነው፤ ዘሮቹ የሌሎች በሆነ ምድር እንደ እንግዳ እንደሚኖሩ፣ የዚያም አገር ሰዎች ባሪያዎች አድርገው 400 ዓመት እንደሚያስጨንቋቸው ነው።
am.R: እግዚአብሔርም ለአብርሃም ሌላ ነገር ነገረው፤ ከእርሱ በኋላ የሚመጣው ቤተሰቡ የእነርሱ ባልሆነ አገር እንደሚኖር ነገረው። የዚያም አገር ሰዎች ባሪያዎች አድርገው 400 ዓመት ክፉኛ እንደሚያስጨንቋቸው ነገረው።

decisions.choice: Genesis 15:13, given as reported speech
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 15:13 closely. Stephen turns them into reported speech, then moves into God's own words in 7:7.

decisions.choice: four hundred years, the figure of Genesis 15:13
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:13 gives 400 years, and Stephen keeps that figure. Exodus 12:40-41 says Israel lived in Egypt 430 years; in the Greek Old Testament and the Samaritan Pentateuch that verse reads "in Egypt and in the land of Canaan". Paul counts 430 years from the promise to the law (Galatians 3:17). The speech quotes the figure of Genesis and does not say how the numbers relate.

decisions.choice: a sojourner: a foreigner living in a land without a citizen's rights
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Moses in Midian (7:29).

decisions.choice: God also told Abraham
decisions.reason: Readable names the one God spoke to.

decisions.choice: make them slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

decisions.choice: quatre cents ans
decisions.reason: The English writes the figure; French running text usually writes a round number like this in words, and the Greek writes it as a word.

decisions.choice: "kiều dân" (L); "người ngoại kiều" (B) for a sojourner
decisions.reason: A foreigner living in a land without a citizen's rights (meaning decision); "kiều dân" is the word of the Vietnamese 1 Peter 1:1.

decisions.choice: "나그네" for paroikos, here and in 7:29; "종으로 삼다" (L, B), "종으로 부리다" (R) for douloō
decisions.reason: A sojourner is a foreigner living in a land without a citizen's rights (meaning decision); "나그네" is the Korean 1 Peter's word for it. Being made slaves is the point here, so the English keeps "slaves"; Korean "종" already says a person owned and made to work, and "노예" would be the stronger alternative.

source.text: καὶ τὸ ἔθνος ᾧ ἐὰν δουλεύσουσιν κρινῶ ἐγώ, ὁ θεὸς εἶπεν, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξελεύσονται καὶ λατρεύσουσίν μοι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ τούτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And the nation to which ever they will serve as slaves will judge I, the God said, and after these things they will come out and will serve me in the place this.

en.L: 'And the nation to which they will be slaves I will judge,' God said, 'and after these things they will come out and serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this place.'
en.B: 'But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves,' God said, 'and afterward they will come out and worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in this place.'
en.R: God said, 'But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. After that, they will leave that country, and they will worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} here in this place.'

es.L: “Y a la nación de la que sean esclavos la juzgaré yo”, dijo Dios, “y después de estas cosas saldrán y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} servirán en este lugar”.
es.B: “Pero yo juzgaré a la nación a la que sirvan como esclavos”, dijo Dios, “y después saldrán y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} adorarán en este lugar”.
es.R: Dios dijo: “Pero yo castigaré a la nación que los haga esclavos. Después de eso saldrán de ese país, y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} adorarán aquí, en este lugar”.

fr.L: “Et la nation dont ils seront esclaves, moi je la jugerai, dit Dieu, et après cela ils sortiront et {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} serviront en ce lieu.”
fr.B: “Mais la nation dont ils seront les esclaves, je la jugerai, dit Dieu, et ensuite ils sortiront et {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} rendront un culte en ce lieu.”
fr.R: Dieu a dit : “Mais je punirai la nation qui fera d’eux des esclaves. Après cela, ils quitteront ce pays et ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}adoreront ici, dans ce lieu.”

sw.L: 'Na taifa lile watakalolitumikia kama watumwa, {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nitalihukumu,' Mungu alisema, 'na baada ya mambo hayo watatoka, nao watanitumikia mahali hapa.'
sw.B: 'Lakini taifa lile watakalolitumikia kama watumwa nitalihukumu,' Mungu alisema, 'na baadaye watatoka, waniabudu mahali hapa.'
sw.R: Mungu alisema, 'Lakini nitaliadhibu taifa litakalowafanya watumwa. Baada ya hapo wataondoka katika nchi hiyo, nao wataniabudu hapa mahali hapa.'

vi.L: Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Còn dân tộc mà họ phải làm nô lệ, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đoán phạt; rồi sau đó họ sẽ ra đi và thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại nơi này.'
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đoán phạt dân tộc đã bắt họ làm nô lệ, và sau đó họ sẽ ra đi và thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại nơi này.'
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ trừng phạt dân tộc bắt họ làm nô lệ. Sau đó, họ sẽ rời khỏi nước ấy và thờ phượng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tại nơi này.'

ko.L: '그리고 그들이 종살이할 그 민족은 내가 심판할 것이다.' 하나님께서 말씀하셨습니다. '그리고 그 뒤에 그들이 나와서 이곳에서 나를 섬길 것이다.'
ko.B: '그러나 그들을 종으로 부린 민족은 내가 심판하겠다.' 하나님께서 말씀하셨습니다. '그 뒤에 그들은 그곳에서 나와 이곳에서 나를 예배할 것이다.'
ko.R: 하나님께서 말씀하셨습니다. '그러나 그들을 종으로 부리는 그 나라는 내가 벌하겠다. 그 뒤에 그들은 그 나라를 떠나, 바로 이곳에서 나를 예배할 것이다.'

pt.L: 'E a nação da qual forem escravos eu julgarei', disse Deus, 'e depois disso sairão e {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} servirão neste lugar.'
pt.B: 'Mas eu julgarei a nação da qual eles forem escravos', disse Deus, 'e depois eles sairão e {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} adorarão neste lugar.'
pt.R: Deus disse: 'Mas eu vou castigar a nação que fizer deles escravos. Depois disso, eles vão sair daquele país e vão {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} adorar aqui neste lugar.'

am.L: “ባሪያ ሆነው የሚገዙለትንም ሕዝብ እኔ እፈርድበታለሁ” አለ እግዚአብሔር፤ “ከዚህም በኋላ ይወጣሉ፤ በዚህም ስፍራ ያገለግሉኛል።”
am.B: “ባሪያ አድርጎ የሚገዛቸውን ሕዝብ ግን እኔ እፈርድበታለሁ” አለ እግዚአብሔር፤ “ከዚያም በኋላ ይወጣሉ፤ በዚህም ስፍራ ያመልኩኛል።”
am.R: እግዚአብሔርም እንዲህ አለ፦ “ባሪያ የሚያደርጋቸውን ሕዝብ ግን እቀጣለሁ። ከዚያ በኋላ ከዚያ አገር ይወጣሉ፤ እዚህ በዚህ ስፍራም ያመልኩኛል።”

decisions.choice: Genesis 15:14: God will judge the nation that enslaves them
decisions.reason: The words follow the Greek Old Testament of Genesis 15:14. The plagues on Egypt are that judgment (Exodus 6:6, 12:12).

decisions.choice: worship me in this place: the words of Exodus 3:12, with the place changed
decisions.reason: Genesis 15:14 ends with the people coming out with great possessions. The last words echo Exodus 3:12, where God tells Moses that the people will serve God "on this mountain". Here it is "this place". It may mean the land where Stephen's hearers live (7:4), or the temple, which the charges called "this place" (6:13-14). The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: serve: serve in worship
decisions.reason: This verb is used of serving God in worship (Luke 2:37, 4:8); the same verb is used in 7:42 of worshiping the stars.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the word that shows this is worship; Literal keeps "serve".

decisions.choice: punish
decisions.reason: Readable says what God's judging the nation would mean for it.

decisions.choice: be slaves / serve as slaves / makes them slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Israel's slavery in Egypt.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} (L)
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself with an emphatic "I" in the Greek; Literal keeps the free pronoun "mimi", which takes the span, as in Acts 13:33, though the English "I" has none.

decisions.choice: "thờ phượng" for "serve" at every level
decisions.reason: Serving God here is serving him in worship (meaning decision); the English Literal keeps "serve", but Vietnamese "phục vụ" would sound like waiting on him.

decisions.choice: "심판하다" (L, B), "벌하다" (R); "섬기다" (L), "예배하다" (B, R) for latreuō
decisions.reason: To serve here is to serve in worship (meaning decision); Literal keeps "섬기다", which also answers "종살이하다" in the same verse, and Balanced and Readable say "worship", as the English does.

decisions.choice: “...” አለ እግዚአብሔር፤ “...” (the speaker between the two parts)
alternatives: one quotation with እግዚአብሔርም እንዲህ አለ before it
decisions.reason: The Greek sets 'God said' inside God's words; Literal and Balanced keep the two parts, with the speaker placed after the first as in the old 'says the Lord' formula, so the quotation keeps its shape. Readable gathers it into one quotation, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ διαθήκην περιτομῆς· καὶ οὕτως ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαὰκ καὶ περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ ὀγδόῃ, καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τὸν Ἰακώβ, καὶ Ἰακὼβ τοὺς δώδεκα πατριάρχας.

records.literal_gloss: And he gave to him a covenant of circumcision; and thus he fathered the Isaac and circumcised him on the day the eighth, and Isaac the Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him a covenant of circumcision. And so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac [fathered] Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
en.B: God also gave him the covenant marked by circumcision. And so, when Isaac was born to Abraham, he circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac in turn had Jacob, and Jacob had the twelve patriarchs.
en.R: God made a covenant with Abraham, and circumcision was the mark of it. So when Abraham's son Isaac was born, Abraham circumcised him when he was eight days old. Later Isaac had a son named Jacob. Jacob had twelve sons, and they were the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel.

es.L: Y le dio un pacto de circuncisión. Y así engendró a Isaac y lo circuncidó al octavo día, e Isaac [engendró] a Jacob, y Jacob a los doce patriarcas.
es.B: Dios también le dio el pacto que tenía como señal la circuncisión. Y así, cuando le nació Isaac, Abraham lo circuncidó al octavo día. Isaac, a su vez, fue padre de Jacob, y Jacob de los doce patriarcas.
es.R: Dios hizo un pacto con Abraham, y la circuncisión era la señal de ese pacto. Por eso, cuando nació Isaac, el hijo de Abraham, Abraham lo circuncidó a los ocho días de nacido. Más tarde Isaac tuvo un hijo llamado Jacob. Jacob tuvo doce hijos, y ellos fueron los padres de las doce tribus de Israel.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui a donné une alliance de circoncision. Et ainsi il a engendré Isaac et l’a circoncis le huitième jour, et Isaac [a engendré] Jacob, et Jacob les douze patriarches.
fr.B: Dieu lui a aussi donné l’alliance marquée par la circoncision. C’est ainsi que, quand Isaac lui est né, Abraham l’a circoncis le huitième jour. Isaac à son tour a eu Jacob, et Jacob a eu les douze patriarches.
fr.R: Dieu a fait une alliance avec Abraham, et la circoncision en était le signe. Alors, quand Isaac, le fils d’Abraham, est né, Abraham l’a circoncis à l’âge de huit jours. Plus tard, Isaac a eu un fils appelé Jacob. Jacob a eu douze fils, et ce sont eux les ancêtres des douze tribus d’Israël.

sw.L: Naye alimpa agano la tohara. Na hivyo akamzaa Isaka, akamtahiri siku ya nane, na Isaka [akamzaa] Yakobo, na Yakobo [akawazaa] wale mababa wakuu kumi na wawili.
sw.B: Mungu alimpa pia agano lenye alama ya tohara. Kwa hiyo Isaka alipozaliwa kwa Ibrahimu, alimtahiri siku ya nane. Isaka naye akamzaa Yakobo, na Yakobo akawazaa wale mababa wakuu kumi na wawili.
sw.R: Mungu alifanya agano na Ibrahimu, na tohara ilikuwa alama ya agano hilo. Kwa hiyo mwana wa Ibrahimu, Isaka, alipozaliwa, Ibrahimu alimtahiri akiwa na umri wa siku nane. Baadaye Isaka alipata mwana aitwaye Yakobo. Yakobo alikuwa na wana kumi na wawili, nao wakawa baba za makabila kumi na mawili ya Israeli.

vi.L: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho ông giao ước cắt bì; và như vậy ông sinh Y-sác và làm lễ cắt bì cho con vào ngày thứ tám; Y-sác [sinh] Gia-cốp, và Gia-cốp [sinh] mười hai tổ phụ.
vi.B: Đức Chúa Trời cũng ban cho ông giao ước có dấu hiệu là phép cắt bì. Vì vậy, khi sinh Y-sác, Áp-ra-ham đã làm lễ cắt bì cho con vào ngày thứ tám. Rồi Y-sác sinh Gia-cốp, và Gia-cốp sinh mười hai tổ phụ.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời lập giao ước với Áp-ra-ham, và phép cắt bì là dấu hiệu của giao ước ấy. Vì vậy khi Y-sác, con trai của Áp-ra-ham, ra đời, Áp-ra-ham làm lễ cắt bì cho con khi được tám ngày. Về sau Y-sác sinh một con trai tên là Gia-cốp. Gia-cốp có mười hai con trai, là tổ tiên của mười hai chi tộc Y-sơ-ra-ên.

ko.L: 그리고 하나님께서 그에게 할례의 언약을 주셨습니다. 그래서 그는 이삭을 낳아 여드레째 되는 날에 그에게 할례를 행하였고, 이삭은 야곱을, 야곱은 열두 족장을 [낳았습니다].
ko.B: 하나님께서는 또 아브라함에게 할례의 언약을 주셨습니다. 그래서 아브라함은 이삭을 낳고 여드레째 되는 날에 할례를 행했습니다. 이삭은 야곱을 낳았고, 야곱은 열두 족장을 낳았습니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서는 아브라함과 언약을 맺으셨고, 할례는 그 언약의 표였습니다. 그래서 아브라함은 아들 이삭이 태어나자 여드레째 되는 날에 할례를 행했습니다. 나중에 이삭은 야곱이라는 아들을 낳았습니다. 야곱은 열두 아들을 낳았는데, 그들은 이스라엘 열두 지파의 조상이 되었습니다.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhe deu uma aliança de circuncisão. E assim ele gerou Isaque e o circuncidou no oitavo dia, e Isaque [gerou] Jacó, e Jacó os doze patriarcas.
pt.B: Deus também lhe deu a aliança marcada pela circuncisão. Assim, quando Isaque nasceu de Abraão, ele o circuncidou no oitavo dia. Isaque, por sua vez, teve Jacó, e Jacó teve os doze patriarcas.
pt.R: Deus fez uma aliança com Abraão, e a circuncisão era o sinal dela. Por isso, quando Isaque, o filho de Abraão, nasceu, Abraão o circuncidou com oito dias de vida. Mais tarde Isaque teve um filho chamado Jacó. Jacó teve doze filhos, e eles foram os pais das doze tribos de Israel.

am.L: የግዝረትንም ቃል ኪዳን ሰጠው፤ እንዲሁም ይስሐቅን ወለደ፤ በስምንተኛውም ቀን ገረዘው፤ ይስሐቅም ያዕቆብን [ወለደ]፤ ያዕቆብም አሥራ ሁለቱን የነገድ አባቶች [ወለደ]።
am.B: እግዚአብሔርም ግዝረት ምልክቱ የሆነውን ቃል ኪዳን ሰጠው። በዚህም መሠረት ይስሐቅ ለአብርሃም በተወለደ ጊዜ በስምንተኛው ቀን ገረዘው። ይስሐቅም ያዕቆብን ወለደ፤ ያዕቆብም አሥራ ሁለቱን የነገድ አባቶች ወለደ።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር ከአብርሃም ጋር ቃል ኪዳን አደረገ፤ የዚህም ቃል ኪዳን ምልክት ግዝረት ነበር። ስለዚህ የአብርሃም ልጅ ይስሐቅ በተወለደ ጊዜ አብርሃም ስምንት ቀን ሲሆነው ገረዘው። በኋላም ይስሐቅ ያዕቆብ የሚባል ልጅ ወለደ። ያዕቆብም አሥራ ሁለት ልጆችን ወለደ፤ እነርሱም የአሥራ ሁለቱ የእስራኤል ነገዶች አባቶች ሆኑ።

decisions.choice: the covenant of circumcision: the covenant of Genesis 17, with circumcision as its mark
decisions.reason: In Genesis 17:9-14 God makes circumcision the sign of the covenant between him and Abraham's family.

decisions.choice: and so: under that covenant, Isaac was circumcised
alternatives: and in this way he became a father
decisions.reason: "So" ties Isaac's circumcision to the covenant just named. Genesis 21:4 says Abraham circumcised Isaac at eight days old, as God had commanded.

decisions.choice: the twelve patriarchs: the twelve sons of Jacob, from whom the tribes of Israel came
decisions.reason: Genesis 35:22-26 and 49:28 list the twelve sons as the heads of the twelve tribes.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the giver of the covenant.

decisions.choice: twelve sons, the fathers of the twelve tribes of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says who the patriarchs were, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: pacto
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for covenant, as in Hebrews and the Gospels: here the covenant of Genesis 17, with circumcision as its mark (m1).

decisions.choice: l’alliance
decisions.reason: The term sheet's word for covenant at every level, Readable included.

decisions.choice: mababa wakuu kumi na wawili (L, B); wana kumi na wawili ... baba za makabila (R)
decisions.reason: The patriarchs are the twelve sons of Jacob from whom the tribes came (meaning decision on the twelve patriarchs). "Baba mkuu" is the word used for a patriarch in Acts 2:29 and Hebrews 7:4, so its plural "mababa wakuu" is used here and in 7:9; Readable explains them as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "mười hai tổ phụ" (L, B) for the twelve patriarchs
decisions.reason: The twelve sons of Jacob, from whom the tribes came (meaning decision); "tổ phụ" is the word used for the patriarch David in 2:29.

decisions.choice: "할례의 언약"; "열두 족장" (L, B), "열두 지파의 조상" (R)
decisions.reason: The covenant of Genesis 17 with circumcision as its mark; the patriarchs are the twelve sons of Jacob (meaning decisions). "할례" and "언약" are the words of the Korean letters; Readable explains, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: የነገድ አባቶች (the patriarchs)
alternatives: ፓትርያርኮች (a word Amharic uses for church patriarchs)
decisions.reason: The twelve patriarchs are the sons of Jacob from whom the tribes came (m3); 'fathers of the tribes' says that, where ፓትርያርክ now names a church office. Readable spells it out, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον· καὶ ἦν ὁ θεὸς μετ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐξείλατο αὐτὸν ἐκ πασῶν τῶν θλίψεων αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ χάριν καὶ σοφίαν ἐναντίον Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου, καὶ κατέστησεν αὐτὸν ἡγούμενον ἐπ’ Αἴγυπτον καὶ ὅλον τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the patriarchs having been jealous of the Joseph sold [him] into Egypt; and was the God with him \v 10 and rescued him out of all the afflictions of him and gave to him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him ruling over Egypt and all the house of him.

en.L: And the patriarchs, being jealous of Joseph, sold [him] into Egypt. And God was with him, \v 10 and rescued him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his house.
en.B: The patriarchs envied Joseph and sold him off to Egypt. Yet God stood by him \v 10 and delivered him from every hardship he met. He gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who made him governor over Egypt and over all his household.
en.R: Jacob's sons were jealous of their brother Joseph. They sold him, and he was taken to Egypt as a slave. But God was with Joseph. \v 10 God rescued him from all his troubles. God made him wise, and Pharaoh the king of Egypt was pleased with him. Pharaoh made Joseph the ruler over Egypt and over everyone in the king's household.

es.L: Y los patriarcas, teniendo celos de José, [lo] vendieron a Egipto. Y Dios estaba con él, \v 10 y lo libró de todas sus aflicciones, y le dio favor y sabiduría delante de Faraón, rey de Egipto, y lo nombró gobernante sobre Egipto y sobre toda su casa.
es.B: Los patriarcas tuvieron envidia de José y lo vendieron para que se lo llevaran a Egipto. Pero Dios estaba con él \v 10 y lo rescató de todas las dificultades que pasó. Le concedió favor y sabiduría ante Faraón, rey de Egipto, que lo hizo gobernador de Egipto y de toda la casa real.
es.R: Los hijos de Jacob tenían celos de su hermano José. Lo vendieron, y se lo llevaron a Egipto como esclavo. Pero Dios estaba con José. \v 10 Dios lo rescató de todos sus problemas. Dios le dio sabiduría, y Faraón, el rey de Egipto, quedó contento con él. Faraón hizo a José gobernador de Egipto y de todos los que vivían en el palacio del rey.

fr.L: Et les patriarches, jaloux de Joseph, [l’]ont vendu pour l’Égypte. Et Dieu était avec lui, \v 10 et l’a délivré de toutes ses afflictions, et lui a donné faveur et sagesse devant Pharaon, roi d’Égypte, et il l’a établi chef sur l’Égypte et sur toute sa maison.
fr.B: Les patriarches, pleins d’envie envers Joseph, l’ont vendu, et il a été emmené en Égypte. Mais Dieu se tenait à ses côtés \v 10 et l’a tiré de toutes les épreuves qu’il a connues. Il lui a accordé faveur et sagesse aux yeux de Pharaon, roi d’Égypte, qui l’a nommé gouverneur de l’Égypte et de toute sa maison.
fr.R: Les fils de Jacob étaient jaloux de leur frère Joseph. Ils l’ont vendu, et il a été emmené en Égypte comme esclave. Mais Dieu était avec Joseph. \v 10 Dieu l’a délivré de tous ses malheurs. Dieu l’a rendu sage, et Pharaon, le roi d’Égypte, l’a apprécié. Pharaon a fait de Joseph le chef de l’Égypte et de tous ceux qui vivaient dans la maison du roi.

sw.L: Na wale mababa wakuu, wakimwonea wivu Yusufu, walimwuza [apelekwe] Misri. Lakini Mungu alikuwa pamoja naye, \v 10 akamwokoa katika dhiki zake zote, akampa kibali na hekima mbele ya Farao mfalme wa Misri, naye akamweka kuwa mtawala juu ya Misri na juu ya nyumba yake yote.
sw.B: Mababa wakuu hao walimwonea wivu Yusufu, wakamwuza akapelekwa Misri. Lakini Mungu alikuwa pamoja naye, \v 10 akamwokoa katika taabu zake zote. Alimpa kibali na hekima mbele ya Farao, mfalme wa Misri, naye Farao akamfanya kuwa mtawala wa Misri na wa watu wote wa nyumba yake.
sw.R: Wana wa Yakobo walimwonea wivu ndugu yao Yusufu. Walimwuza, naye akapelekwa Misri kama mtumwa. Lakini Mungu alikuwa pamoja na Yusufu. \v 10 Mungu alimwokoa katika taabu zake zote. Mungu alimpa hekima, na Farao mfalme wa Misri akapendezwa naye. Farao alimfanya Yusufu kuwa mtawala wa Misri na wa watu wote wa nyumba ya mfalme.

vi.L: Các tổ phụ vì ghen ghét Giô-sép nên đã bán ông sang Ai Cập; nhưng Đức Chúa Trời ở với ông, \v 10 giải cứu ông khỏi mọi hoạn nạn, và ban cho ông được ơn và khôn ngoan trước mặt Pha-ra-ôn, vua Ai Cập; và vua lập ông làm tể tướng cai trị Ai Cập và cả cung điện mình.
vi.B: Các tổ phụ ghen ghét Giô-sép nên bán ông sang Ai Cập. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời ở cùng ông, \v 10 giải cứu ông khỏi mọi hoạn nạn. Ngài ban cho ông được ơn và khôn ngoan trước mặt Pha-ra-ôn, vua Ai Cập, và vua lập ông làm tể tướng cai trị Ai Cập và cả hoàng gia.
vi.R: Các con trai của Gia-cốp ghen ghét em mình là Giô-sép. Họ bán Giô-sép, và ông bị đem sang Ai Cập làm nô lệ. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời ở với Giô-sép. \v 10 Đức Chúa Trời giải cứu ông khỏi mọi khó khăn. Đức Chúa Trời ban cho ông sự khôn ngoan, và Pha-ra-ôn, vua Ai Cập, rất hài lòng về ông. Pha-ra-ôn lập Giô-sép làm người cai trị Ai Cập và mọi người trong hoàng gia.

ko.L: 그리고 족장들은 요셉을 시기하여 [그를] 이집트에 팔아 버렸습니다. 그러나 하나님께서 그와 함께 계셔서, \v 10 그의 모든 환난에서 그를 건져 내시고, 이집트 왕 바로 앞에서 그에게 은혜와 지혜를 주셨습니다. 그래서 [바로가] 그를 이집트와 자기 온 집을 다스리는 사람으로 세웠습니다.
ko.B: 족장들은 요셉을 시기하여 그를 이집트에 팔아넘겼습니다. 그러나 하나님께서 요셉과 함께 계셨습니다. \v 10 하나님께서는 그를 모든 고난에서 건져 주시고, 이집트 왕 바로 앞에서 은총과 지혜를 주셨습니다. 그래서 바로는 그를 이집트와 자기 왕궁 전체를 다스리는 총리로 세웠습니다.
ko.R: 야곱의 아들들은 자기들의 동생 요셉을 시기했습니다. 그래서 요셉을 팔아 버렸고, 요셉은 종이 되어 이집트로 끌려갔습니다. 그러나 하나님께서 요셉과 함께 계셨습니다. \v 10 하나님께서는 요셉을 모든 어려움에서 건져 주셨습니다. 하나님께서 요셉을 지혜롭게 하시니, 이집트 왕 바로가 요셉을 좋아하게 되었습니다. 바로는 요셉을 이집트와 왕궁의 모든 사람을 다스리는 사람으로 세웠습니다.

pt.L: E os patriarcas, tendo inveja de José, [o] venderam para o Egito. E Deus estava com ele \v 10 e o livrou de todas as suas aflições, e lhe deu graça e sabedoria diante de Faraó, rei do Egito, e este o constituiu governador sobre o Egito e sobre toda a sua casa.
pt.B: Os patriarcas tiveram inveja de José e o venderam para o Egito. Mas Deus estava com ele \v 10 e o livrou de todas as aflições que ele passou. Deu-lhe favor e sabedoria diante de Faraó, rei do Egito, que o nomeou governador do Egito e de todo o seu palácio.
pt.R: Os filhos de Jacó tinham inveja do irmão deles, José. Eles o venderam, e José foi levado para o Egito como escravo. Mas Deus estava com José. \v 10 Deus o livrou de todos os seus problemas. Deus o fez sábio, e Faraó, o rei do Egito, gostou dele. Faraó fez José governador do Egito e de todos os que viviam no palácio do rei.

am.L: የነገድ አባቶችም በዮሴፍ ቀንተው ወደ ግብፅ ሸጡት፤ እግዚአብሔርም ከእርሱ ጋር ነበረ፤ \v 10 ከመከራውም ሁሉ አዳነው፤ በግብፅ ንጉሥ በፈርዖን ፊትም ሞገስንና ጥበብን ሰጠው፤ በግብፅና በቤቱ ሁሉ ላይም ገዥ አድርጎ ሾመው።
am.B: የነገድ አባቶች በዮሴፍ ቀንተው ወደ ግብፅ ሸጡት። እግዚአብሔር ግን ከእርሱ ጋር ነበር፤ \v 10 ከደረሰበትም መከራ ሁሉ አዳነው። በግብፅ ንጉሥ በፈርዖን ፊት ሞገስና ጥበብ ሰጠው፤ ፈርዖንም በግብፅና በቤቱ ሁሉ ላይ ገዥ አድርጎ ሾመው።
am.R: የያዕቆብ ልጆች በወንድማቸው በዮሴፍ ቀኑበት። ሸጡትም፤ እርሱም ባሪያ ሆኖ ወደ ግብፅ ተወሰደ። እግዚአብሔር ግን ከዮሴፍ ጋር ነበር። \v 10 ከመከራውም ሁሉ አዳነው። እግዚአብሔር ጥበብ ሰጠው፤ የግብፅ ንጉሥ ፈርዖንም በእርሱ ደስ ተሰኘ። ፈርዖን ዮሴፍን በግብፅና በንጉሡ ቤተሰብ ሁሉ ላይ ገዥ አደረገው።

decisions.choice: the story of Joseph in Genesis 37-41
decisions.reason: His brothers were jealous of him (Genesis 37:11) and sold him (37:28); God was with him (39:2, 39:21); Pharaoh saw his wisdom and set him over Egypt and his house (41:37-44; see also 45:8).

decisions.choice: favor: the goodwill God won for Joseph in Pharaoh's eyes
decisions.reason: The word is the one often translated grace, but here it means favor in the eyes of a person, as in Genesis 39:21, where God gave Joseph favor with the keeper of the prison.

decisions.choice: he appointed him: Pharaoh made Joseph ruler
decisions.reason: The subject changes from God to Pharaoh, as in Genesis 41:41-43.

decisions.choice: the brothers rejected the one God was with
alternatives: a story with no wider point
decisions.reason: Joseph's brothers turn against him, yet God is with him and he becomes their rescuer. The speech shows the same pattern in Moses (7:25, 7:35) and comes at last to Jesus (7:52).

decisions.choice: Jacob's sons ... their brother Joseph ... as a slave
decisions.reason: Readable says who the patriarchs were and that Joseph was sold as a slave (Genesis 37:28, 39:1).

decisions.choice: Pharaoh ... was pleased with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what favor before Pharaoh means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: favor
decisions.reason: The word here is the goodwill God won for Joseph in Pharaoh's eyes (m2), not grace that saves, so Spanish says "favor" and keeps "gracia" for grace.

decisions.choice: "được ơn" (L, B) for favor
decisions.reason: The goodwill God won for Joseph in Pharaoh's eyes (meaning decision), not "ân điển", as in the Vietnamese Luke 2:52.

decisions.choice: "Giô-sép", "Pha-ra-ôn"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms.

decisions.choice: "요셉", "바로"; "은혜" (L), "은총" (B) for charis here; "[바로가]" (L)
decisions.reason: "바로" is the Protestant form for Pharaoh, as in the Korean Romans 9:17. Charis here is the goodwill God won for Joseph in Pharaoh's eyes (meaning decision), so Balanced says "은총" and keeps the key term "은혜" for God's grace; Literal keeps the key term. He who appointed him is Pharaoh (meaning decision), which Korean must say.

decisions.choice: "동생 요셉" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names Joseph as their brother, as the English Readable does; Joseph was younger than the brothers who sold him, so Korean says "동생".

decisions.choice: Faraó, as a name, without article
decisions.reason: Brazilian Bible usage treats "Faraó" as the king's name in these stories, without an article, as the stated list of names for this chapter has it; "o faraó" would read as a history book.

source.text: ἦλθεν δὲ λιμὸς ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν Αἴγυπτον καὶ Χανάαν καὶ θλῖψις μεγάλη, καὶ οὐχ ηὕρισκον χορτάσματα οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Came then a famine upon all the Egypt and Canaan and affliction great, and not were finding food the fathers of us.

en.L: Then a famine came over all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers were not finding food.
en.B: Then famine struck the whole of Egypt and Canaan, bringing great hardship, and our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} could find nothing to eat.
en.R: Then there was a famine in all of Egypt and Canaan. People suffered terribly. Our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} could not find any food.

es.L: Llegó entonces una hambruna sobre todo Egipto y Canaán, y una gran aflicción, y nuestros padres no encontraban sustento.
es.B: Luego una hambruna azotó todo Egipto y Canaán, y causó gran sufrimiento; nuestros {{gender:antepasados|padres}} no podían encontrar nada que comer.
es.R: Después hubo hambruna en todo Egipto y en Canaán. La gente sufría muchísimo. Nuestros {{gender:antepasados|padres}} no podían encontrar comida.

fr.L: Or une famine est survenue sur toute l’Égypte et Canaan, et une grande détresse, et nos pères ne trouvaient pas de nourriture.
fr.B: Puis une famine a frappé toute l’Égypte et Canaan, causant une grande détresse, et nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} ne trouvaient rien à manger.
fr.R: Puis il y a eu une famine dans toute l’Égypte et dans le pays de Canaan. Les gens ont terriblement souffert. Nos {{gender:ancêtres|pères}} ne trouvaient rien à manger.

sw.L: Kisha njaa ikaja juu ya Misri yote na Kanaani, na dhiki kubwa, na baba zetu hawakupata chakula.
sw.B: Kisha njaa ilitokea katika nchi yote ya Misri na Kanaani, ikaleta dhiki kubwa, na mababu zetu hawakuweza kupata chakula.
sw.R: Kisha kulikuwa na njaa katika nchi yote ya Misri na Kanaani. Watu waliteseka sana. Mababu zetu hawakuweza kupata chakula chochote.

vi.L: Bấy giờ có nạn đói và hoạn nạn lớn xảy đến trên khắp xứ Ai Cập và Ca-na-an, và tổ phụ chúng ta không tìm được lương thực.
vi.B: Rồi nạn đói xảy ra khắp xứ Ai Cập và Ca-na-an, gây nên cảnh khốn khổ lớn, và tổ tiên chúng ta không tìm được gì để ăn.
vi.R: Rồi có nạn đói khắp xứ Ai Cập và Ca-na-an. Dân chúng chịu khổ rất nhiều. Tổ tiên chúng ta không tìm được thức ăn.

ko.L: 그런데 온 이집트와 가나안에 흉년이 들어 큰 환난이 닥쳤고, 우리 조상들은 먹을 것을 찾지 못했습니다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 온 이집트와 가나안에 흉년이 들어 큰 고난이 닥쳤습니다. 우리 조상들은 먹을 것을 구할 수가 없었습니다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 이집트와 가나안 온 땅에 흉년이 들었습니다. 사람들은 몹시 고생했습니다. 우리 조상들도 먹을 것을 찾을 수 없었습니다.

pt.L: Então veio uma fome sobre todo o Egito e Canaã, e grande aflição, e os nossos pais não encontravam alimento.
pt.B: Então veio uma fome sobre todo o Egito e Canaã, trazendo grande sofrimento, e os nossos {{gender:antepassados|pais}} não conseguiam achar o que comer.
pt.R: Depois houve fome em todo o Egito e em Canaã. O povo sofreu muito. Os nossos {{gender:antepassados|pais}} não conseguiam encontrar comida.

am.L: በግብፅና በከነዓን ሁሉ ላይ ራብና ታላቅ መከራ መጣ፤ አባቶቻችንም ምግብ አያገኙም ነበር።
am.B: ከዚያም በግብፅና በከነዓን ሁሉ ራብ ገባ፤ ታላቅ መከራም አመጣ፤ {{gender:ቅድመ አያቶቻችንም|አባቶቻችንም}} የሚበሉት አጡ።
am.R: ከዚያም በግብፅና በከነዓን ሁሉ ራብ ሆነ። ሰዎች እጅግ ተሠቃዩ። {{gender:ቅድመ አያቶቻችን|አባቶቻችን}} ምንም ምግብ ሊያገኙ አልቻሉም።

decisions.choice: the famine of Genesis 41-42
decisions.reason: Genesis 41:54-57 and 42:5 tell of the famine over Egypt and Canaan.

decisions.choice: food: provisions, anything to live on
decisions.reason: The word was first used of food for animals, but by this time it meant food in general.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Here "fathers" means the whole household of Jacob, men and women; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: nuestros padres (L); nuestros {{gender:antepasados|padres}} (B, R)
alternatives: antepasados with no setting, as John 6:31
decisions.reason: As in Hebrews and in the English: the forebears, men and women. Literal keeps the Greek word "padres"; Balanced and Readable say "antepasados" and let the reader choose the traditional "padres". The same through the chapter (7:19, 32, 38-39, 44-45, 51-52); where only the sons of Jacob are meant (7:12, 15), "antepasados" takes no span.

decisions.choice: baba zetu (L); mababu zetu (B, R), no gender span
decisions.reason: As in Acts 3:13 and 13:17: "mababu" (forebears) is the ordinary Swahili word for the ancestors of a nation and already takes in women and men, so the English ancestors / fathers span has no Swahili counterpart; Literal keeps "baba" as the English Literal keeps "fathers". The same wherever the fathers recur in this speech.

decisions.choice: "조상들" with no gender span, through Stephen's speech
decisions.reason: "조상" means forebears, women and men alike, as in 3:13, so the English span has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: antepassados, with "pais" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As the English, where "fathers" means the earlier generations of Israel, men and women. Where it means particular men, Jacob's sons (7:12, 7:15), Portuguese says "antepassados" with no setting, since the word fits them as well.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ቅድመ አያቶቻችን|አባቶቻችን}} (our ancestors, or our fathers)
decisions.reason: Where the English Balanced and Readable put 'our fathers' meaning the earlier generations of Israel under the gender setting, Amharic has the same two ways of saying it: ቅድመ አያቶች, 'ancestors', and the traditional አባቶች, 'fathers'. The span mirrors the English through Stephen's speech, with any suffix or prefix inside each option; Literal keeps አባቶች, and 'our fathers' meaning Jacob's sons (7:12, 7:15) has no span.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ Ἰακὼβ ὄντα σιτία εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἐξαπέστειλεν τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν πρῶτον·

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then Jacob being grain into Egypt he sent out the fathers of us first;

en.L: But when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers [the] first [time].
en.B: When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our forefathers there on a first journey.
en.R: Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt. So he sent his sons, our forefathers, to buy some. This was their first trip.

es.L: Pero al oír Jacob que había grano en Egipto, envió a nuestros padres [la] primera [vez].
es.B: Cuando Jacob oyó que había grano en Egipto, envió allá a nuestros antepasados en un primer viaje.
es.R: Jacob oyó que había grano en Egipto. Por eso envió allá a sus hijos, nuestros antepasados, para comprar un poco. Ese fue su primer viaje.

fr.L: Mais Jacob, ayant appris qu’il y avait du blé en Égypte, a envoyé nos pères une première [fois].
fr.B: Quand Jacob a appris qu’il y avait du blé en Égypte, il y a envoyé nos pères une première fois.
fr.R: Jacob a appris qu’il y avait du blé en Égypte. Alors il a envoyé ses fils, nos ancêtres, pour en acheter. C’était leur premier voyage.

sw.L: Lakini Yakobo aliposikia kwamba kuna nafaka Misri, aliwatuma baba zetu mara ya kwanza.
sw.B: Yakobo aliposikia kwamba kulikuwa na nafaka Misri, aliwatuma mababu zetu huko safari ya kwanza.
sw.R: Yakobo alisikia kwamba kulikuwa na nafaka Misri. Kwa hiyo aliwatuma wanawe, mababu zetu, waende kununua. Hiyo ilikuwa safari yao ya kwanza.

vi.L: Nghe nói ở Ai Cập có lúa, Gia-cốp sai tổ phụ chúng ta đi lần thứ nhất.
vi.B: Khi Gia-cốp nghe ở Ai Cập có lúa, ông sai tổ phụ chúng ta đến đó lần thứ nhất.
vi.R: Gia-cốp nghe nói ở Ai Cập có lúa. Vì vậy ông sai các con trai mình, là tổ phụ chúng ta, đi mua lúa. Đó là chuyến đi thứ nhất của họ.

ko.L: 그러나 야곱은 이집트에 곡식이 있다는 말을 듣고, 우리 조상들을 처음으로 보냈습니다.
ko.B: 야곱은 이집트에 곡식이 있다는 말을 듣고 우리 조상들을 처음으로 그곳에 보냈습니다.
ko.R: 야곱은 이집트에 곡식이 있다는 말을 들었습니다. 그래서 곡식을 사 오라고 자기 아들들, 곧 우리 조상들을 그곳에 보냈습니다. 그것이 그들의 첫 번째 길이었습니다.

pt.L: Mas Jacó, ouvindo que havia trigo no Egito, enviou os nossos pais [pela] primeira [vez].
pt.B: Quando Jacó ouviu que havia trigo no Egito, enviou para lá os nossos antepassados numa primeira viagem.
pt.R: Jacó ouviu dizer que havia trigo no Egito. Por isso mandou os filhos dele, os nossos antepassados, comprar um pouco. Essa foi a primeira viagem deles.

am.L: ያዕቆብም በግብፅ እህል እንዳለ ሰምቶ አባቶቻችንን በመጀመሪያ [ጊዜ] ላካቸው።
am.B: ያዕቆብ በግብፅ እህል እንዳለ በሰማ ጊዜ አባቶቻችንን ለመጀመሪያ ጉዞ ወደዚያ ላካቸው።
am.R: ያዕቆብ በግብፅ እህል እንዳለ ሰማ። ስለዚህ አባቶቻችን የሆኑትን ልጆቹን እህል እንዲገዙ ላካቸው። ይህ የመጀመሪያ ጉዞአቸው ነበር።

decisions.choice: Genesis 42:1-3: Jacob sends his sons for grain
decisions.reason: Jacob sent ten of his sons and kept Benjamin at home (Genesis 42:3-4).

decisions.choice: our fathers: here the sons of Jacob
decisions.reason: The ones Jacob sent to Egypt were his sons, named men (Genesis 42:3), the forefathers of the tribes.

decisions.choice: our forefathers, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Here the word means particular men, the sons of Jacob, so the inclusive setting does not apply; "forefathers" says that plainly.

decisions.choice: his sons ... to buy some
decisions.reason: Readable names those sent and why they went (Genesis 42:2).

decisions.choice: nuestros antepasados, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Here "our fathers" are the sons of Jacob (m2), men only, so as in the English there is no gender setting.

decisions.choice: "tổ phụ chúng ta" at every level for "our fathers", here the sons of Jacob
decisions.reason: These fathers are named men, the sons of Jacob (meaning decision), and the English drops its setting here; "tổ phụ" names forefathers who are men.

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ ἀνεγνωρίσθη Ἰωσὴφ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς αὐτοῦ, καὶ φανερὸν ἐγένετο τῷ Φαραὼ τὸ γένος Ἰωσήφ.

records.literal_gloss: and on the second was made known Joseph to the brothers of him, and known became to the Pharaoh the family of Joseph.

en.L: And on the second [visit] Joseph was made known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh.
en.B: On their second visit Joseph let his brothers know who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.
en.R: When they went to Egypt the second time, Joseph told his brothers who he was. And Pharaoh found out about Joseph's family.

es.L: Y en la segunda [visita] José se dio a conocer a sus hermanos, y el linaje de José llegó a ser conocido por Faraón.
es.B: En la segunda visita, José les hizo saber a sus hermanos quién era, y Faraón se enteró de cuál era la familia de José.
es.R: Cuando fueron a Egipto por segunda vez, José les dijo a sus hermanos quién era. Y Faraón supo de la familia de José.

fr.L: Et lors de la seconde [visite], Joseph s’est fait reconnaître par ses frères, et la famille de Joseph est devenue connue de Pharaon.
fr.B: Lors de leur second voyage, Joseph a révélé à ses frères qui il était, et Pharaon a été informé de la famille de Joseph.
fr.R: Quand ils sont retournés en Égypte la deuxième fois, Joseph a dit à ses frères qui il était. Et Pharaon a découvert la famille de Joseph.

sw.L: Na katika [safari] ya pili Yusufu alijulikana kwa ndugu zake, na ukoo wa Yusufu ukajulikana kwa Farao.
sw.B: Katika safari yao ya pili Yusufu aliwajulisha ndugu zake yeye ni nani, na Farao akapata habari za jamaa ya Yusufu.
sw.R: Walipokwenda Misri mara ya pili, Yusufu aliwaambia ndugu zake yeye ni nani. Naye Farao akapata habari kuhusu jamaa ya Yusufu.

vi.L: Và lần thứ hai, Giô-sép tỏ cho các anh mình biết mình là ai, và Pha-ra-ôn biết được gia đình của Giô-sép.
vi.B: Trong chuyến đi thứ hai, Giô-sép cho các anh mình biết mình là ai, và Pha-ra-ôn biết về gia đình của Giô-sép.
vi.R: Khi họ đến Ai Cập lần thứ hai, Giô-sép nói cho các anh mình biết ông là ai. Và Pha-ra-ôn biết được gia đình của Giô-sép.

ko.L: 그리고 두 번째에 요셉이 자기 형제들에게 알려졌고, 요셉의 가족이 바로에게 알려졌습니다.
ko.B: 그들이 두 번째로 갔을 때에 요셉이 형들에게 자기가 누구인지 밝혔고, 바로도 요셉의 가족에 관하여 알게 되었습니다.
ko.R: 그들이 두 번째로 이집트에 갔을 때에, 요셉은 형들에게 자기가 누구인지 말했습니다. 그리고 바로도 요셉의 가족에 관하여 알게 되었습니다.

pt.L: E na segunda [vez] José se deu a conhecer aos seus irmãos, e a família de José tornou-se conhecida de Faraó.
pt.B: Na segunda viagem, José revelou aos irmãos quem ele era, e Faraó ficou sabendo da família de José.
pt.R: Quando eles foram ao Egito pela segunda vez, José contou aos irmãos quem ele era. E Faraó ficou sabendo da família de José.

am.L: በሁለተኛውም [ጉዞ] ዮሴፍ ለወንድሞቹ ታወቀ፤ የዮሴፍም ወገን ለፈርዖን ታወቀ።
am.B: በሁለተኛው ጉዞአቸው ዮሴፍ ማን እንደ ሆነ ለወንድሞቹ ገለጠላቸው፤ ፈርዖንም ስለ ዮሴፍ ቤተሰብ አወቀ።
am.R: ለሁለተኛ ጊዜ ወደ ግብፅ በሄዱ ጊዜ ዮሴፍ ማን እንደ ሆነ ለወንድሞቹ ነገራቸው። ፈርዖንም ስለ ዮሴፍ ቤተሰብ አወቀ።

decisions.choice: Genesis 45: Joseph makes himself known
decisions.reason: Joseph revealed himself to his brothers on their second journey (Genesis 45:1-4), and Pharaoh heard that Joseph's brothers had come (45:16).

decisions.choice: was made known: Joseph made himself known to them
decisions.reason: The passive verb can mean that Joseph let himself be known, as Genesis 45:1 says.

decisions.choice: their second visit
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "on the second"; Balanced and Readable supply the journey meant.

decisions.choice: "các anh mình" for Joseph's brothers
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say older or younger; in Genesis all but Benjamin were older than Joseph, and it was they who came.

decisions.choice: "형제들" (L), "형들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The brothers who came were older than Joseph, as Genesis tells it; Balanced and Readable say so, where Literal keeps the Greek's plain "brothers".

source.text: ἀποστείλας δὲ Ἰωσὴφ μετεκαλέσατο Ἰακὼβ τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν συγγένειαν ἐν ψυχαῖς ἑβδομήκοντα πέντε, καὶ κατέβη Ἰακὼβ εἰς Αἴγυπτον.

records.literal_gloss: Having sent then Joseph called for Jacob the father of him and all the kindred in souls seventy-five; \v 15 and went down Jacob into Egypt.

en.L: Then Joseph sent and summoned Jacob his father and all [his] relatives, seventy-five souls in all. \v 15 And Jacob went down into Egypt.
en.B: Joseph sent for his father Jacob and for all his relatives, seventy-five people in all, \v 15 and Jacob went down to Egypt.
en.R: Joseph sent a message to his father Jacob. He asked him to come to Egypt with the whole family. There were seventy-five of them. \v 15 So Jacob went down to Egypt.

es.L: Entonces José mandó llamar a Jacob su padre y a toda [su] parentela, setenta y cinco almas en total. \v 15 Y Jacob descendió a Egipto.
es.B: José mandó a buscar a su padre Jacob y a todos sus parientes, setenta y cinco personas en total, \v 15 y Jacob bajó a Egipto.
es.R: José envió un mensaje a su padre Jacob. Le pidió que viniera a Egipto con toda la familia. Eran setenta y cinco personas. \v 15 Así que Jacob bajó a Egipto.

fr.L: Alors Joseph a envoyé chercher Jacob son père et toute [sa] parenté, soixante-quinze âmes. \v 15 Et Jacob est descendu en Égypte.
fr.B: Joseph a fait venir son père Jacob et toute sa parenté, soixante-quinze personnes en tout, \v 15 et Jacob est descendu en Égypte.
fr.R: Joseph a envoyé un message à son père Jacob. Il lui a demandé de venir en Égypte avec toute la famille. Ils étaient soixante-quinze. \v 15 Alors Jacob est descendu en Égypte.

sw.L: Kisha Yusufu akatuma [watu], akamwita Yakobo baba yake na jamaa yote, nafsi sabini na tano. \v 15 Naye Yakobo akashuka Misri.
sw.B: Yusufu alituma watu kumwita Yakobo baba yake pamoja na jamaa zake wote, watu sabini na watano kwa jumla, \v 15 naye Yakobo akashuka Misri.
sw.R: Yusufu alimtumia baba yake Yakobo ujumbe. Alimwomba aje Misri pamoja na jamaa yote. Walikuwa watu sabini na watano. \v 15 Kwa hiyo Yakobo alishuka Misri.

vi.L: Giô-sép sai người mời Gia-cốp, cha mình, và cả gia đình, tổng cộng bảy mươi lăm người. \v 15 Rồi Gia-cốp xuống Ai Cập.
vi.B: Giô-sép sai người mời cha là Gia-cốp và cả họ hàng, tất cả là bảy mươi lăm người, \v 15 và Gia-cốp xuống Ai Cập.
vi.R: Giô-sép gửi lời đến cha mình là Gia-cốp. Ông mời cha cùng cả gia đình đến Ai Cập. Họ có tất cả bảy mươi lăm người. \v 15 Vậy Gia-cốp xuống Ai Cập.

ko.L: 그리고 요셉은 사람을 보내어 자기 아버지 야곱과 온 친족, 일흔다섯 명을 불렀습니다. \v 15 그래서 야곱이 이집트로 내려갔습니다.
ko.B: 요셉은 사람을 보내어 아버지 야곱과 온 친족 일흔다섯 명을 불러들였습니다. \v 15 그래서 야곱은 이집트로 내려갔습니다.
ko.R: 요셉은 아버지 야곱에게 사람을 보냈습니다. 그리고 온 가족과 함께 이집트로 오시라고 했습니다. 그들은 모두 일흔다섯 명이었습니다. \v 15 그래서 야곱은 이집트로 내려갔습니다.

pt.L: E José mandou chamar Jacó, seu pai, e toda a [sua] parentela, setenta e cinco almas [ao todo]. \v 15 E Jacó desceu ao Egito.
pt.B: José mandou buscar seu pai, Jacó, e todos os seus parentes, setenta e cinco pessoas ao todo, \v 15 e Jacó desceu ao Egito.
pt.R: José mandou um recado a seu pai, Jacó. Pediu que ele viesse ao Egito com toda a família. Eram setenta e cinco pessoas. \v 15 Então Jacó desceu ao Egito.

am.L: ዮሴፍም ልኮ አባቱን ያዕቆብንና ዘመዶቹን ሁሉ፣ ሰባ አምስት ነፍስ የሆኑትን አስጠራ፤ \v 15 ያዕቆብም ወደ ግብፅ ወረደ።
am.B: ዮሴፍም ልኮ አባቱን ያዕቆብንና ዘመዶቹን ሁሉ አስጠራ፤ በአጠቃላይ ሰባ አምስት ሰዎች ነበሩ። \v 15 ያዕቆብም ወደ ግብፅ ወረደ።
am.R: ዮሴፍ ወደ አባቱ ወደ ያዕቆብ መልእክት ላከ። ከቤተሰቡ ሁሉ ጋር ወደ ግብፅ እንዲመጣ ጠየቀው። እነርሱም ሰባ አምስት ሰዎች ነበሩ። \v 15 ስለዚህ ያዕቆብ ወደ ግብፅ ወረደ።

decisions.choice: seventy-five persons, the number in the Greek Old Testament
alternatives: seventy, the number in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text gives the number of Jacob's family who came to Egypt as seventy (Genesis 46:27; Exodus 1:5; Deuteronomy 10:22). The Greek Old Testament gives seventy-five in Genesis 46:27 and Exodus 1:5, counting more of Joseph's descendants (Greek Genesis 46:20). A Hebrew manuscript of Exodus from Qumran also reads seventy-five in Exodus 1:5. Stephen gives the number found in the Greek. The counts also differ in whom they include: Genesis 46:26 gives sixty-six. Reviewers should check the Qumran reading.

decisions.choice: in souls: persons, people
decisions.reason: "Souls" here simply counts people, as in 2:41.

decisions.choice: Genesis 45:9-11 and 46:1-7
decisions.reason: Joseph sent for his father, and Jacob went down to Egypt with all his family.

decisions.choice: sent a message ... asked him to come to Egypt
decisions.reason: Readable says what Joseph's sending meant.

decisions.choice: "일흔다섯 명" (L) for "in seventy-five souls"
decisions.reason: In souls means persons (meaning decision); as in 2:41, Korean "영혼" would suggest the soul apart from the body.

source.text: καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν, καὶ μετετέθησαν εἰς Συχὲμ καὶ ἐτέθησαν ἐν τῷ μνήματι ᾧ ὠνήσατο Ἀβραὰμ τιμῆς ἀργυρίου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἑμμὼρ ἐν Συχέμ.

records.literal_gloss: and died he and the fathers of us, \v 16 and they were carried over to Shechem and were placed in the tomb which bought Abraham for a price of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.

en.L: And he died, he and our fathers, \v 16 and they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
en.B: There he died, and so did our forefathers. \v 16 They were carried back to Shechem and laid in the tomb Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor at Shechem.
en.R: Jacob died there. Our forefathers, his sons, died there too. \v 16 Later they were carried back to Shechem. They were buried in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor in Shechem. He had paid for it with silver.

es.L: Y murió él, y nuestros padres, \v 16 y fueron trasladados a Siquem y puestos en el sepulcro que Abraham había comprado por una suma de plata a los hijos de Hamor en Siquem.
